title: Hearty Sour Argentinian Beef Empanadas
description: A traditional Argentinian dish featuring sour and aerated beef empanadas, perfect for a weeknight dinner
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, white vinegar, chopped onion, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper, mixing well with your hands until just combined.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight to allow the flavors to meld.
Soak the corn husks in water for at least 30 minutes to make them pliable.
To assemble the empanadas, lay a corn husk flat on a work surface and place about 1/4 cup of the beef mixture in the center of the husk.
Fold the sides of the husk over the filling and then roll the empanada up, starting from the wide end.
Repeat with the remaining corn husks and beef mixture.
In a large skillet, heat about 1/2 inch of beef broth over medium heat and add the empanadas, seam-side down.
Cook the empanadas for about 5 minutes on each side, or until they are lightly browned and the filling is cooked through.
Serve the empanadas hot, garnished with chopped fresh cilantro if desired.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
